recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13130 unless Patient Care opens a new issue to revisit planned, not-yet-initiated Communication scope after FHIR-28235.
issue_request: FHIR-13130 was a Published Patient Care change request for FHIR-core Communication, raised against DSTU2 and applied for DSTU2. It asked to clarify whether Communication may be used for planned, in-progress, or failed communications; the final Persuasive with Modification resolution added the planned/failed scope sentence, clarified the nurse-notification recipient, and added an inability-to-deliver-lab-results use case.
initial_application: Commit bac396f21d6dc845c746e29a9fb7c79e27ee6ff5 applied the issue on 2017-05-11 by changing the Communication introduction to say the resource is a record even if planned or failed, adding the on-call physician recipient to the nurse notification example, and adding the unable-to-deliver-lab-results example. Later Communication edits for FHIR-17902 and FHIR-13389 retained the failed-delivery example while refining surrounding use-case wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists communication=Communication as an active resource, so the inspected Communication narrative and StructureDefinition files are current build inputs. Later Applied Communication issues changed the timing sentence: FHIR-28235, applied by 40aa5c88300a803dc5d821194e74821ab60e2340 and reconciled on the combined branch by 5bba6cd7bce30a882d0b330b45cb073265ac2e9d, replaced the literal planned/failed phrase with 'has occurred or where the communication process has at least initiated.' FHIR-40760 and its reconciliation preserved the same later wording in Boundaries and Relationships. The current StructureDefinition still supports failed communications through Communication.status = not-done and statusReason for reasons a communication did not happen.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is warranted because the current narrative includes the clarified recipient wording and the inability-to-deliver-lab-results example, and the conformance source supports failed/not-done communications. Restoring the older literal planned wording would conflict with the later FHIR-28235 Patient Care decision.
